topics.topic: Which accepted owner actions and transitions have OwnerAuditAction rows or deliberately produce no audit entry
questions: Does OWNER_AUDIT_ACTIONS contain rows only for owner actions that create an audit entry, or must every accepted owner action have a row, including reads and other actions that write no audit entry?
Which accepted owner actions and conditional transitions have rows, including which owner actions deliberately write no audit entry?
What is the complete mapping from accepted owner actions, customer transitions and project-erasure kinds to audit actions, including which accepted actions write no audit entry?

quotes:
- the change: which action, in a closed vocabulary State 6 declares. The
  actions that write an entry (R0-58): creating, correcting, archiving,
  anonymising and deleting a project; recording, correcting and erasing a
  customer; restricting and lifting; ending and resuming a relationship;
  granting a project to a session and revoking one; the import, as one entry
  naming the migration closure (M10) by its file digest; erasing old entries. An answer
  to an access request that grants a project writes the grant's entry; a
  decline changes no session's projects and only clears the request (R0-64),
  so it writes none (R0-58; codex round-01 T4). No entry is written for adding a
  room, publishing or withdrawing a pointer, registering a session, an access
  request or its decline, changing or clearing the active project, or any read
  (R0-58). Anonymising or deleting a project writes that one entry; the
  project leaving every session's granted set (R0-61) is its consequence and
  writes no revocation entry (owner, 2026-10-31; codex round-02 T6);

A row of the owner audit table: which audit action (M09, R0-58) an accepted
owner action writes — for a customer mark, by its transition; for a project's
erasure, by its kind (owner, 2026-11-24).
judgement.why: M09 exhaustively identifies the state-changing actions that write entries and the reads and other actions that do not, while M28 states that its rows map those audited owner actions, customer transitions and project-erasure kinds to their audit actions.

topics.topic: Which product action creates or replaces UploadedFile
questions: Is uploading a file a distinct product action that creates or replaces M21, or is M21 created only as an internal step of the confirmed import action?
Which product action creates or replaces M21: a separate upload action, the import action itself, or the action that displays import confirmation?

quotes:
`module:owner_sessions`. Keep an accepted upload in the session's memory,
replacing the session's earlier one (A16 rule 2).

`module:operations`. Run one owner request: sign-in and sign-out, the
confirmation step, the upload and the mapping, and every owner action in
its one transaction with its entry and confirmation id (A04, A13, A14, A16).
judgement.why: The later public APIs make upload a distinct owner request whose accepted upload creates or replaces the session's UploadedFile before any confirmation step.

topics.topic: Which target, version, digest, and upload identity facts a pending confirmation binds
questions: Does a pending import confirmation bind only the uploaded bytes' digest, or does it also bind the UploadedFile upload number so that a later upload of identical bytes is distinguishable?
For each confirmation-producing product action, which target, version and input-digest facts must M20 contain?

quotes:
The admitted session; the action; its target; the revision or access
version the step shows, or that it shows none; the action's inputs — for an
erasure its choice, for the import the upload's number and the file's
digest with the picks, names, aliases and Customer values, for an erasure
of old entries the date.

The session's pending confirmation is replaced: a new value from
`random_values.make_secret_value`, bound to the action, its target, what the
step showed and the digest of its inputs in a fixed order, and the reading
of `clock.monotonic_reading` it was shown at.
judgement.why: The later session API enumerates the target, revision or access-version state and action-specific inputs, and expressly includes both upload number and file digest in an import confirmation's binding.

topics.topic: Who assigns an upload number, when, and from what state it is derived
questions: Who derives the digest and who assigns the upload number, and is the number derived from the sequence of upload events in that owner session?
Who assigns the upload number, when is it assigned, and from what state is it derived?

quotes:
The admitted session, holding the import lock and its own lock; the file's
bytes and the digest `migration_import.read_import_mapping` computed of them
when it accepted them.

The upload's number in the session: 1 for the session's first accepted
upload, then one more than the session's last, so two uploads of the same
bytes are two uploads (A16 rule 2).
judgement.why: The later APIs say migration_import computes the digest from accepted bytes and owner_sessions assigns a monotonically increasing session-local number to each accepted upload.

topics.topic: When a submission attempt consumes or clears PendingConfirmation
questions: Does “used” clear the pending confirmation on every submission attempt, only after its value is successfully validated, or only after the confirmed product action is accepted?

quotes:
It is valid only in that session, while
less than 10 minutes have passed since it was shown, and is used up by the first submission that carries it, whatever
its answer; a refused submission needs the step shown again. A submission
carries it when it passes the owner session and CSRF checks (A04 rule 6,
stage 1) and gives a value equal to the pending one; from there on,
whatever the answer — a binding to another action or input included — the
pending value is used up. A submission refused before those checks, or
giving another value while the pending one is still valid, is refused and
leaves it as it was. A submission that passes those checks when the
pending one has expired is refused and clears it, whatever value it
gives.
judgement.why: State 2 specifies exactly which submissions consume, preserve or clear the pending confirmation, including consumption by a later-refused product action.

topics.topic: Whether redisplaying a confirmation reuses or replaces PendingConfirmation
questions: When the same confirmation page is shown again, does Registry read the existing PendingConfirmation or create and replace it with a new value?

quotes:
at most one pending confirmation — its one-time value, the action, its
target, the revision or access version if the step showed one, and the
inputs it is bound to, and
the instant it was shown — made when a confirmation step is shown, replaced
by the next one shown and cleared when used;
judgement.why: Every showing makes a PendingConfirmation and the next showing replaces it, so redisplaying the step creates a replacement rather than merely reading the existing value.
